speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs how is Singapore handling the different practices and ideologies in the name of Islam especially in the context of the emergence of groups such as Islam Nusantara.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: So, too, for Islam and our Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS would engage such groups to counsel them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS has instituted policies that seek to manage diversity, particularly in the regulation of religious activities in mosques.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Through Friday sermons and religious classes, the Muslim public is encouraged to be civil and respectful when dealing with intra-faith differences.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Through various initiatives organised by MUIS, mosques and Muslim organisations, different segments of the community come together and work on common projects and, in so doing, build community cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: What we must guard against are ideologies and practices that divide our community and which set our community against the rest of society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For instance, MUIS provides guidelines to ensure that mosques serve as safe and open spaces for all Muslims.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We do not tolerate those who sow discord and create divisions between Singapore Muslims and other communities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Indeed, there is no place for exclusivist and extremist doctrines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The RRG comprises local Islamic scholars who offer advice and counselling.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Now, more than ever, we need our community leaders and religious teachers to speak out against ideologies that create divisions within Islam and between Islam and the wider society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: If they do not do so, their silence may be regarded as a tacit endorsement of such doctrines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Everyone in our community must work together to safeguard our way of life and the values that our community cherishes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I just find out if we are able to do more in terms of educational publicity, reaching out to some of the groups which may not be formal?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Some of them may inadvertently not realise that they are being taught some of these variants of the religion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are not against informal groups as many find it convenient to organise these based on their needs and demands on their time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If they can do that, it would be good.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thus far, the list has been well-publicised and well-utilised.
